newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends higher on bullish temp forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends higher on bullish temp forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices rose Monday on forecasts of below normal temperatures amid an expected decline in refined product output, said traders.
"It looks like we are going to have freezing weather this week which has given the market impetus to trade back up," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products for Paribas Futures Inc.
February heating oil settled up 0.52 cent at 67.29 cents a gallon. March crude ended off 11 cents a barrel at $23.94 while February gasoline finished 0.13 cent a gallon lower at 67.62 cents.
"There is a good case for refined products. Production is expected to decline with the refinery turnarounds, but crude continues to weigh down the market due to weak cash prices," said Kevelson.
A slew of refineries in the U.S. Gulf have shut production for seasonal maintenance during January and February.

Meanwhile, Weather Services Corp forecasted below normal temperatures this week in the northeastern United States, the largest heating oil market in the world. The National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast called for normal to below normal temperatures in the region starting January 30.
Dealers noted prompt crude was particulary vulnerable technically after closing below $24.00 for the first time since mid-December.

"The level of open interest for crude is really quite modest," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group. He noted the relative lack of short positions which decreases the potency of any short covering rally in crude.
As of January 24, open interest for crude was down 2,591 at 347,692.
Still, March crude's session low of $23.63 bounced off the top of a price gap between $23.62 and $23.56 made on December 16, creating support, dealers said.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
